messages.subject: [R-sig-ME] Fit CS and Ar1 in lme4
messages.subject_clean: Fit CS and Ar1 in lme4
messages.body_plain:
Not sure why, but I have always imagined that lme4 standard notation was
using CS, not US correlation.



Can someone please tell me how to fit these models using *cs*, and *ar1*? This
was a n-of-1 trial (single subject) consisting of four cycles. Each cycle
included two 2-week treatment periods (aka, "order" variable), totaling 4
weeks per cycle. Data for the outcomes were collected during the final five
days of each 2-week period.



m1 <- lmer(pain_global ~ treat + (1 | cycle), data = dat)

m2 <- lmer(pain_global ~ treat + (1 | cycle/order), data = dat)



I got the idea that it was not as simple as just adding cs or ar1.



If necessary, the ordering variable is *day*.   dat <- dat[order(dat$cycle,
dat$day), ]



Df below. Thank you





# Download the file from GitHub (use raw download URL)

url <- "
https://github.com/jorgemmteixeira/databases/raw/main/n1_lyrica_v2.xlsx"

temp <- tempfile(fileext = ".xlsx")

download.file(url, temp, mode = "wb")



# Read into R

dat <- read_excel(temp)



dat <- dat %>%

  mutate(

    date    = as.Date(date),



    # treat: 0 = Off Lyrica (reference), 1 = On Lyrica

    treat   = factor(treat, levels = c(0, 1),

                     labels = c("Nothing", "Lyrica")),



    # cycle and order as factors (for fixed-effect use later) AND as
integers

    cycle   = factor(cycle),

    order   = factor(order)

  )





library(lme4)

m1 <- lmer(pain_global ~ treat + (1 | cycle), data = dat)


m2 <- lmer(pain_global ~ treat + (1 | cycle/order), data = dat)

messages.subject_clean: Fit CS and Ar1 in lme4
messages.body_plain:
This might get you started. PLEASE INSTALL THE DEVELOPMENT VERSION OF
lme4 (`remotes::install_github("lme4/lme4")`), there are some relevant
bug fixes ...

library(lme4)
m1 <- lmer(pain_global ~ treat + (1 | cycle), data = dat)
m2 <- lmer(pain_global ~ treat + (1 | cycle/order), data = dat)
m3 <- lmer(pain_global ~ treat + cs(0+order | cycle),
           data = dat)
summary(select(dat, c(cycle, order, day)))

m4 <- lmer(pain_global ~ treat + ar1(0+factor(day) | cycle,
                                     hom = TRUE),
           data = dat)
m5 <- lmer(pain_global ~ treat + cs(0+factor(day) | cycle,
                                    hom = TRUE),
           data = dat, verbose = TRUE)

with(dat, table(day, cycle))
library(bbmle)
mlist <- list(int_only = m1, "cycle/order" = m2, "cs(order|cycle)" =
m3, "cs()"  = m4, "ar1()" = m5)
AICtab(mlist,
       logLik = TRUE)

## AICtab is *too* aggressive in rounding log-likelihoods, we want to
see the differences ...
nll <- sapply(mlist, logLik)
round(nll - min(nll), 3)

messages.subject: [R-sig-ME] Online course: Generalized Linear Mixed Models (GLMMs) in R
messages.subject_clean: Online course: Generalized Linear Mixed Models (GLMMs) in R
messages.body_plain:
Dear all,
 
We are pleased to announce an upcoming online course on Generalized Linear Mixed Models (GLMMs) in R, taking place from 21?24 September.
 
Course website: [ https://www.physalia-courses.org/courses-workshops/glmms-in-r/ ]( https://www.physalia-courses.org/courses-workshops/glmms-in-r/ ) 
 
In this course, participants will learn how to specify, interpret, and validate GLMMs in R, with a strong focus on practical applications using the lme4 and glmmTMB packages. The course emphasizes how to build statistically sound and defensible models for real research data.
 
The course is intended for researchers and graduate students with prior experience in regression models in R who want to extend their skills to mixed models and more advanced modelling frameworks. 
Over four days (14:00?19:00 Berlin time), the program will cover:
Day 1: Regression fundamentals, interactions, contrasts, ANOVA, and model misspecification
Day 2: Random effects, variance structures, model selection, and causal vs predictive approaches
Day 3: GLMM formulation, interpretation, diagnostics, and model validation (including DHARMa)
Day 4: Spatial, temporal, and phylogenetic correlation structures in GLMMs
The course will combine lectures, discussions, and hands-on exercises via Zoom and Slack.
By the end of the course, participants will be able to confidently build, interpret, and validate GLMMs and apply them appropriately in their own research.
 
If you want to get introduced to GLMs in R, have a look at this course: [ https://www.physalia-courses.org/courses-workshops/glm-in-r-1/ ]( https://www.physalia-courses.org/courses-workshops/glm-in-r-1/ ) 
 
We look forward to your participation.
Best regards, Carlo
--------------------

Carlo Pecoraro, Ph.D


Physalia-courses DIRECTOR

info at physalia-courses.org

mobile: +49 17645230846

[ Bluesky ]( https://bsky.app/profile/physaliacourses.bsky.social ) [ Linkedin ]( https://www.linkedin.com/in/physalia-courses-a64418127/ )
